answers.answer: Shuffle the four Conflict III cards and place all four face down at the bottom. Shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five face down on top of those. Shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one face down on top. The resulting 10-card deck is one I, five II, and four III, with I on top. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: A human starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game. In either player count, they have two Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; 12 troop cubes total, with three troops in their garrison and the other nine in supply; and they take 1 water.
answers.evidence: Components: ‘16 cubes’ per player, of which four start on Influence and the ‘other 12 cubes are troops.’ Setup, step 6: place three troops in the garrison; score on 1 in a 4-player game or 0 otherwise; put two Agents on the Leader and the third beside the board; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain. After you Reveal, your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the cards remaining in your hand that you reveal, not cards already played on Agent turns. During Clean Up, move all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’ and ‘Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Reveal Turn: ‘just-revealed cards only (not of cards played on Agent turns)’; Clean Up moves ‘all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.’

answers.answer: No. You must pay the destination’s costs immediately before resolving any effects of the space or the card, so an Agent-turn card effect cannot first provide resources for that entry cost. One card can send only one Agent, using only one of its Agent icons. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs ‘immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played)’; ‘You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents’; ‘A card with no Agent icons can't be played on an Agent turn.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited during the current turn can deploy, plus up to two from the garrison, for up to five deployed troops total. At a non-Combat space, recruited troops go to the garrison and cannot deploy there. Troops are recruited from your supply; recruited troops are placed in your garrison before any Combat-space deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: a cube icon recruits from supply and places a troop in the garrison. At a Combat space you may deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn … plus up to two more units from your garrison.’

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; that use does not recall the Spy. Infiltrate is a separate option when sending an Agent: recall your Spy from a connected post to ignore another player’s Agent and use that same occupied space. Gather Intelligence is also optional when sending an Agent: recall a connected Spy to draw a card, choosing immediately after placing the Agent and before receiving space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both; you may use two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement, but not use two Spies to Gather Intelligence on that placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: the Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a connected space and ‘do not recall the Spy’; Infiltrate recalls a Spy to use an occupied space; Gather Intelligence is chosen ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects)’; ‘You cannot recall the same Spy to both’ effects. FAQ & Rulings: two Spies may be recalled for different effects, never two to Gather Intelligence on the same placement.

answers.answer: The strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm contributes 3, and four revealed swords contribute 4. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0, even with swords. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window, which is for players with at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; ‘You must have at least one unit in the Conflict to have any strength; if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0.’ Combat Intrigue is for each player with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict.’

answers.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent you from playing later in the Combat Intrigue phase. The window closes once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively; then Combat resolves. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not their garrison), and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier in the phase’; resolve when all involved players ‘pass consecutively.’ After rewards, troops return to ‘supply (not their garrison)’ and sandworms to ‘the bank.’

answers.answer: In both cases, tied players for first each receive the second reward, and no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card. In a three-player game, no other rewards are given. In a four-player game with exactly two tied for first, the remaining players compete for the third reward; if three or more tie for first, no other rewards are given. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players each gain the second reward and ‘no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card.’ With three or fewer players no other rewards; with four, exactly two tied first means remaining players compete for third. Resolve Combat: ‘A player with 0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double the rewards you take; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward that offers 3 spice to gain 1 VP, the summary says you may pay the cost a second time to gain the effect a second time: pay another 3 spice for another VP, or 6 spice total for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘if you have one or more sandworms … double the rewards’; control and battle icons cannot be doubled. Optional reward costs may be paid a second time; example: ‘pay 3 spice to gain 1 VP, or 6 spice to gain 2.’

answers.answer: After you win and take the Conflict card into your supply, check for a normal battle-icon match. A matching face-up Conflict or Objective card qualifies. If there is a match, matching is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During the Endgame, the wild battle icon may be matched with any one of the three battle icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the card, ‘check if you have another face-up Conflict or Objective card’ with the same icon; if so, you ‘must’ flip the pair for 1 VP. During Endgame, match the wild icon with any of the three icons.

answers.answer: Reaching 2 Influence gives 1 VP, which is lost if you drop below 2. Reaching 4 gives the bonus shown on that track space, which is retained if you later drop below 4. The first player to reach 4 takes that Faction’s Alliance token and its VP; merely tying the holder at 4 does not take the Alliance, because an opponent must rise to a higher space to pass the holder. The FAQ says if the holder later loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes it (or the former holder chooses among multiple tied players); falling to 3 or lower also loses the Alliance.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: reaching 2 gives 1 VP, lost below 2; reaching 4 grants a bonus not given back below 4. The Alliance goes to the first at 4 and passes when an opponent rises to a ‘higher’ space. FAQ & Rulings: after the holder loses Influence from a tie, the formerly tied player takes the Alliance; falling to 3 or lower also loses it.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent during the Reveal turn to acquire cards, including before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources to buy one card and split Persuasion from one source across cards. After buying a Row card, its replacement is immediately available for acquisition if you can afford it. The acquired card goes face up into your discard pile and is not used right away.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: use gained Persuasion to acquire cards ‘before, between, or after’ Reveal effects. Acquiring Cards: Persuasion may be pooled or split; the Row replacement can be acquired ‘if you can afford it’; an acquired card goes face up into the discard pile.

answers.answer: At the end of each round in Makers, put 1 bonus spice on each Maker space without an Agent; it accumulates with bonus spice left from prior rounds. When you send an Agent to a Maker space, gain all bonus spice there. A sandworm may be summoned only if you have a Maker Hooks token when required, and not to a Conflict protected by the Shield Wall; removing the Shield Wall allows sandworms at any Conflict. A summoned sandworm is immediately deployed to your Conflict quadrant and can never be placed in a garrison. Maker Hooks are retained, not spent, when summoning.
answers.evidence: Makers: add 1 spice to each Agent-free Maker space; when visited, gain ‘all the bonus spice there.’ Sandworms: Maker Hooks requirement; Shield Wall blocks summoning at the three protected locations; sandworm goes into the Conflict and ‘can never be placed in a garrison.’ FAQ: Hooks are retained.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, reaching 10 or more VP or having an empty Conflict deck triggers the Endgame. Players first may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare VP. Tiebreakers are, in order: spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘At the end of a round’ the threshold or empty deck triggers Endgame; first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then the most VP wins. Tiebreakers: ‘amount of spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.’

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup uses the 20 standard contracts: shuffle them, reveal two face up, and place the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add four additional Intrigue cards and four additional Imperium cards to their respective decks. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and stay out of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: shuffle ‘the 20 contracts,’ flip two up and place ‘the remaining 18 face down’; shuffle four additional Intrigue and four additional Imperium cards into their decks; Shaddam is an option. Components and CHOAM section identify the 10 contrasting-back contracts as Rise of Ix only and say to leave them in the box for standard CHOAM.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts, put it in your supply, and replace it with a contract from the bank flipped face up. If all contracts have been taken, the icon gives 2 Solari instead. A Harvest contract requires sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the stated amount of spice that turn in total, including spice from other sources. The Immediate contract completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: the icon takes a face-up contract and replaces it; if all are taken it reverts to 2 Solari. Completing contracts specifies the Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow completion conditions.

answers.answer: No. If you gain a contract for a board space after already sending your Agent there that turn, you must wait for a future turn; you must have held the contract when sending the Agent. When you complete it, announce it, gain its printed rewards, then flip the token face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: if you take a contract for a space where you ‘already sent your Agent this turn,’ wait until a future turn and ‘must have had the contract at the time you sent the Agent.’ On completion, ‘announce it, gain the rewards it shows, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.’

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the two eligible remaining Objectives are dealt randomly to the humans. The First Player marker goes to the human whose Objective shows it. The round’s turn order is First Player → Rival → other human, with First Player alternating only between humans. The Rival takes Agent turns while it has an Agent and never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: ‘one shared scoring Rival’; give it the Ornithopter Objective and deal the other two to humans; First Player goes to the matching human. Rival is immediately clockwise from First Player; it ‘never takes a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: If a revealed House Hagal destination is occupied, ignore it and reveal again until an Agent can be placed on an unoccupied indicated space. A Place Spy card uses an empty post of its specified type; if none exists, ignore Spy placement, and either way reveal another Hagal card because the Rival has not sent an Agent. The Rival ignores ordinary board-space costs and effects and applies only the revealed House Hagal effects. If the House Hagal deck empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore an occupied destination and reveal again. Spies and Schemes: Place Spy uses an empty post of its specified type, or ignores placement if none; either way reveal another card because no Agent was sent. Rival rules: ignore normal space costs/effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
